clue.text: Evidently most of the people are employed with it, and it should be enough to get things accomplished.

definitions.text: Evidently most of the people are employed with it, and it should be enough to get things accomplished.

parts.words: Evidently most of the people are employed
parts.note: read literally, the larger share of people being in jobs is a majority that is working
the real sense: a parliamentary margin big enough to pass legislation

explanation.surface: A remark about full employment that seems to promise a productive economy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half plays on the words taken literally; the second gives the political sense of a government's majority large enough to carry its business.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics this phrase names a majority in a legislature large enough to pass bills reliably.

clue.text: In reach, if you want to grab something.

definitions.text: In reach, if you want to grab something.

parts.note: the plain sense: close enough to be attained

parts.words: if you want to grab something
parts.note: the literal picture: the thing is near enough for your hand to close on it

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for being attainable, and the clue adds its literal sense of a hand closing on an object.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning attainable or achievable, literally close enough for a hand to seize.

clue.text: Concerning malice, you get a delay for a time.

parts.note: re is the business-letter word meaning about or concerning
spite is the wish to hurt someone

explanation.surface: A spiteful act seems to buy someone a temporary postponement.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short interval of relief or a temporary reprieve from something unpleasant.

clue.text: In short, I am what the throbbing type does, having sudden inclinations.

parts.note: contracted, as 'In short' tells you, to I'm
something throbbing pulses, beating rhythmically

explanation.surface: Someone with a throbbing pulse admits to being given to whims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' asks for the contraction of 'I am', dropping the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Impulses are sudden urges or whims to act without forethought.

clue.text: Get a different opening?

indicators.note: the letters of 'Get a' are made different by being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether to try another way in.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is an opening in a wall or fence that can be closed.

clue.text: Staying away from something can get nonappearance around it.

indicators.note: the word for nonappearance is placed around 'it', meaning the can just mentioned

parts.note: absence is failing to appear
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Avoiding something can amount to simply never turning up near it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is the practice of refraining from something, such as drink.

clue.text: The writer has nothing on a layer that goes to the little railroad.

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
a hen is a bird that lays eggs
RY is a short form of railway

explanation.surface: A writer seems to put an egg-layer on a toy train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The little railroad' asks for an abbreviation rather than a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: O. Henry was the pen name of the American short-story author William Sydney Porter.

clue.text: Urged to get what the firm often is, in short–and tied-untied.

parts.words: what the firm often is, in short
parts.note: a firm is often incorporated, shortened to Inc.

indicators.note: the word tied is loosened, its letters shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pushed into incorporating a company and in knots about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir someone up or encourage them to act.

clue.text: It is said to have something that is ancient and true blue–which does a lot of spouting.

definitions.text: It is said to have something that is ancient and true blue–which does a lot of spouting.

parts.words: something that is ancient and true blue
parts.note: ancient is old and true blue is faithful, giving the name of a famous geyser
the geyser erupts regularly, spouting water high in the air

explanation.walkthrough: Old Faithful, the geyser, is spelt out as 'ancient' plus 'true blue'; the answer is the place said to contain it.
explanation.definitionFit: This US national park in Wyoming is home to the Old Faithful geyser and many others.

clue.text: A heavy drinker is one coming back to place.

indicators.note: the word for one such drinker is read backwards

parts.note: one heavy drinker, that is a sot
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: A drunkard keeps returning to his usual haunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' points back to the heavy drinker, so it stands for a sot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosspot is an old word for a habitual drunkard.

clue.text: Confused clients may be used for letters or other designs.

definitions.text: may be used for letters or other designs
definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun: what may be used for lettering

indicators.note: the letters of clients are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Muddled customers might be scribbling letters and doodles.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out sheet through which paint is applied to reproduce lettering or patterns.

clue.text: Here in Paris it makes a clean start, but is rather drippy.

definitions.note: describes the thing, a noun that drips

parts.note: ici is French for here
the start of the word clean, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A Parisian claims a fresh beginning while being rather wet.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a hanging spike of ice that drips as it melts.

clue.text: If you have words and music, this is the first part.

definitions.text: If you have words and music, this is the first part.

parts.note: an opera or musical is made of a text and a score
words come first in the phrase, so the answer is the text of the work

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is on word order: in 'words and music' the words are named first.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera or musical, written to be set to music.

clue.text: Little expeditions around Rio, in a way, to find something that's just for girls!

indicators.note: the little expeditions are placed around the rearranged Rio

parts.note: sorties are short raids or excursions

indicators.note: Rio is rendered in another way, its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Short trips around Rio de Janeiro make an outing reserved for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Sororities are women-only student societies at US colleges.

clue.text: Pogo's home!

parts.note: Pogo is the possum hero of Walt Kelly's comic strip, not a pogo stick
where the strip's characters live

explanation.walkthrough: A pogo stick would have no home; Pogo the comic-strip possum lives in a famous swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The Okefenokee Swamp on the Georgia–Florida border is the setting of the Pogo comic strip.

clue.text: Does badly at poetry.

definitions.note: a mass noun standing for the plural: poems

indicators.note: the word Does is written out badly, its letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone performs poorly when it comes to verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, so a set of them is poetry.

clue.text: A place in California where a fool comes up with a study on a combination of it.

indicators.note: in a down answer the study sits on top of the final letter
in a down answer, coming up means reading the words from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
a sap is a fool
a den is a private study
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Californian town where an idiot turns up to study a combination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'of it' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city near Los Angeles, home of the Rose Bowl.

clue.text: Goes out like the tide.

parts.note: recedes or falls away
the sea's water flowing back from the shore

explanation.walkthrough: A nearly straight definition: the verb for a tide flowing out.
explanation.definitionFit: When a tide retreats from the shore it is said to fall back in this way.

clue.text: If you get to libel a scoffer, a famous showman will turn up.

indicators.note: the name appears, turning up inside the run of words libel a scoffer

parts.note: the words the name is found inside

explanation.surface: Defame a mocker and a celebrated impresario will appear.
explanation.walkthrough: David Belasco was a celebrated American theatre producer and playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: David Belasco was a renowned Broadway producer famous for spectacular stagecraft.

clue.text: Rather iffy. (To you, sounds like Mr. Charlie has 500 to go!)

indicators.note: the clue says only the sound of to you is wanted, not its spelling

parts.note: the words to you, run together in speech, give the opening sound of the answer
Charlie Chan, the detective of novels and films
taken as written

explanation.surface: An uncertain situation explained as a sum about a man and 500 to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals; Charlie Chan was a famous fictional detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch-and-go describes something risky whose outcome is uncertain.

clue.text: This should be a helluva game!

definitions.text: This should be a helluva game!

parts.note: devilish, pointing to the Spanish diablo, devil, inside the name
a juggling game spinning a two-headed top on a string

explanation.walkthrough: The name looks like the word for devil, so the game is hellish in name at least.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling toy spun on a cord between two sticks.

clue.text: How you got wild game, even with a bad, bad egg to show for it.

definitions.note: a description rather than a verb: you got it by doing what the answer says

indicators.note: the letters are spoiled like a rotten egg, so mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hunter's trip with only a rotten egg to show for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter who has bagged game has caught or shot it.

clue.text: Terribly vain gal with an average grade is shocking!

indicators.note: the words vain gal are terribly mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
C is the middle mark on a school report

explanation.surface: A conceited girl scraping a mediocre mark causes outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanic means producing electric current, and figuratively jolting or startling.

clue.text: Your friend had dinner, which is what made him enjoy it.

definitions.note: a description standing for a noun: the sense of taste

parts.note: a pal is a friend
ate is had a meal

explanation.surface: A friend dined well, and his taste buds made it a pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: The palate is the sense of taste, so it is what lets one relish food.

clue.text: Possibly cups of fish from the Atlantic.

indicators.note: a possible arrangement of the letters of cups

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps cups made of seafood from the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The scup is a porgy found along the North American Atlantic coast.

clue.text: What the Bantu might throw in the grass again.

indicators.note: the weapon sits inside the words the grass again

parts.note: the words the answer is found in

explanation.surface: A spear tossed back into the grass by a Bantu hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: An assagai is a slender iron-tipped throwing spear of southern Africa.

clue.text: Can more possibilities exist where famous violins are made?

indicators.note: other possible arrangements of these letters exist

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wonder whether more options exist in a violin-making town.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremona in northern Italy is the city of the Stradivari, Amati and Guarneri luthiers.

clue.text: Exhibiting the condition of the gal in 22!

definitions.text: Exhibiting the condition of the gal in 22!

parts.note: showing off a state of mind
clue 22 speaks of a vain gal, so her condition is vanity

explanation.walkthrough: Clue 22 begins 'Terribly vain gal', so the condition is vanity and the answer is a simile for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile for extreme vanity, after the strutting bird famous for showing off its tail.
